full_judgment: 9. Mr Sk. Reajul Hogue learned Advocate appearing with Ms. Shishirkona, learned Advocate for the petitioners submits that the Court of appeal, upon misreading and non-consideration of the evidence and misconception of law illegally allotted 0.1250 acre land in the saham of the plaintiff though her vendors had transferable right of 0.0250 acre land and in doing so did not discuss any evidence of the parties. Learned Advocate further submits that as the last court of facts, the Court of appeal did not evaluate or discuss any evidence independently and come to independent findings of fact or reversed the findings of fact of the trial Court but illegally reversed the judgment and decree of the trial Court. Learned Advocate further submits that the Court of appeal erroneously held that complicated question of title is involved in the suit and a simple suit for partition is not maintainable but it decided the suit on merit and decreed the suit. Learned Advocate further submits that upon amicable partition among the RS recorded tenants, Mozaffar and others got 0.20 acre land out of 0.50 acre suit land and transferred the same to Amena Khatun by registered deed of pattan dated 21-2-1947 being No. 1259 and on the strength of said pattan separate SA Khatian No. 363 was prepared and finally published in the name of Amena Khatun and accordingly, the said pattan has been acted upon and title of 0.20 acre land vested to Amena Khatun, who thereafter, transferred the same to Abul Fazal Kha vide registered sale date dated 4-7-1962 and accordingly, the RS recorded tenants and their successors lost their title to 0.20 acre land. Learned Advocate further submits that defendant Nos. 1-2 acquired title to 0.20 acre land through Amena Khatun by successive transfers through valid registered sale deeds and mutated their names in respect of 0.20 acre land and have been owning and possessing the same for more than 12 years and accordingly, they have acquired adverse possession in respect of said 0.20 acre land. Learned Advocate further submits that by deed No. 3250 dated 8-3-1967 though 0.50 acre land was shown to have been transferred to Sultan, Abdur Razzak, Enaruddinn and Aneruddin but the vendors of said deed had title to and transferable right of only 0.30 acre land and after deduction of 0.20 acre land, Sultan and three others acquired title to 0.0750 acre land each instead of 0.1250 acre land each. Learned Advocate further submits that after transfer of 0.1250 acre land to Taijuddin by Sultan and Razzak by registered sale deed dated 26-4-1972 they had title to only 0.0250 acre instead of 0.1250 acre land and accordingly, the plaintiff got title to only 0.0250 acre land from Sultan and Abdur Razzak by sale deed No. 3176 dated 8-3-1976. Learned Advocate further submits that the trial Court upon evaluation of evidence of the parties came to the conclusion that the plaintiff is entitled to 0.0250 acre land but the Court of appeal without discussing any evidence of the defendant Nos. 1-2 illegally reduced their share to 0.3525 acre from 0.4525 acre land and illegally increased share of the plaintiff from 0.0250 acre land to 0.1250 acre land. Learned Advocate finally submits that the impugned judgment is not a proper judgment of reversal and, as such, liable to be set-aside.
